diagnostics.message: :data.aws_ecs_task_definition.this: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_ecs_task_definition.this is redundant — already implied by attribute references

:data.aws_ecs_task_definition.this already depends on :resource.aws_ecs_task_definition.this implicitly through its `task_definition = aws_ecs_task_definition.this[0].family` attribute reference, which already forces the task definition to be created before the data source is read. The explicit `depends_on = [aws_ecs_task_definition.this]` duplicates that dependency and is redundant.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.this sets `enable_execute_command = var.enable_execute_command` and launches tasks that assume the tasks IAM role (:resource.aws_iam_role.tasks). When ECS Exec is enabled, those tasks need the `ssmmessages:*` permissions granted by the inline policy :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.tasks at launch time, but no attribute reference or depends_on orders the service after that policy — on a first apply the tasks can start before the policy exists/propagates and `ecs exec` will fail until a redeployment. The service should depend on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.tasks.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition sets `enable_execute_command = var.enable_execute_command` and launches tasks that assume the tasks IAM role. When ECS Exec is enabled, the tasks require the `ssmmessages:*` permissions from the inline policy :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.tasks at launch time, but nothing orders this service after that policy — tasks may start before the policy is in place and ECS Exec will fail until the tasks are redeployed. The service should depend on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.tasks.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.this launches the tasks defined by :resource.aws_ecs_task_definition.this, whose containers rely on the task execution role for pulling ECR images, writing CloudWatch logs, and reading secrets/SSM parameters. The service only waits for the *service* role policy attachment (aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service) and has no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec, so on a first apply tasks can launch before the execution-role policy is attached/propagated, causing transient ImagePull/log/secret initialization failures. The service should depend on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition launches the tasks defined by the task definition, whose containers rely on the task execution role for pulling ECR images, writing CloudWatch logs, and reading secrets/SSM parameters. Nothing orders this service after :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec, so tasks can launch before the execution-role policy is attached/propagated, causing transient task startup failures on first apply. The service should depend on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec.
